Project overview

The Placewise loyalty programme existed exclusively in the native mobile app — with a long-outdated visual design. This project brought it to the web — responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop — while refreshing the look and rebuilding it on a variables-based system, so that admins can apply full module branding directly from MPC.

Designed end-to-end: from kickoff and architecture decisions through 6 service pages, multi-state user flows, and full handoff to 3 teams simultaneously. Now in active development and already sold to clients based on the prototype.

01 — Understanding

Product
Definition

Placewise clients — shopping centres across Europe and the US — had a loyalty programme running in their native mobile apps. Their websites had none of it. Members visiting the mall website couldn't check points, browse rewards, or redeem anything.

The goal: bring the full rewards module to the web, built responsively, embeddable as blocks within the existing Website → Page → Block architecture of MPC.

The gap
App-only loyalty

The rewards programme was locked inside the native app. Website visitors — a significant share of total audience — had no access to their loyalty status or rewards.

The opportunity
Single codebase, 3 surfaces

Building as a shared web component means it serves the mall website, mobile webview, and webforms — all from one codebase, branded per client.

The constraint
Fit the existing CMS

The module had to follow the Website → Page → Block convention in MPC. Service pages provisioned automatically, blocks configurable per page.

02 — Research

From app
to web.

The native mobile app was the primary reference — proven UX that users were familiar with. The research phase focused on what needed to change when moving from native to responsive web.

Native app as baseline
What changes on web
  • Bottom tab bar → horizontal tab row at top of content
  • Native modals → web-native confirmation dialogs
  • System push → web push / email notifications
  • Design works across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints
Key decisions
Architecture & integration
  • Integration model from OCR module — iframe with branding extension
  • Application Branding variables — colours and tokens inherited per client
  • Anonymous user strategy: public rewards visible without login
  • Module is the seed for the European website template
Competitive moodboard — loyalty & rewards apps

04 — Outcome

Handoff
& beyond.

Complete handoff to three teams simultaneously. The interactive Figma prototype was used directly in client sales conversations — the module is being sold before development ships.

Frontend handoff
Web & responsive specs
  • All 6 service pages across 3 breakpoints
  • Component annotations for block variants and states
  • Branding token mapping to Application Branding variables
  • Interaction specs for modals, timers, state transitions
Backend handoff
Data & API requirements
  • Page-by-page data requirements per block
  • User state logic — content rules for all 3 auth states
  • Closest reward algorithm spec
  • Coupon use flow — timer, state update, fraud prevention
Mobile team handoff
Webview integration
  • Navigation behaviour within native app shell
  • iframe integration pattern (same model as OCR module)
  • Push notification link targets
Prototype flows — used in client sales demos
Scope expanded after client feedback.

After the initial design was presented, client feedback pushed us to extend the final step of the reward redemption flow — not only a countdown timer for showing the coupon to the cashier, but also a QR code scan option.

The change was delivered as a client-level variant and shipped to production.

My personal takeaway

This project was particularly interesting because we cared deeply about visual consistency across different endpoints — web, mobile webview, and webforms had to feel like one product. Connecting the end user experience with the way admin users configure those same views in MPC was the real design challenge: every decision had to make sense from both sides of the screen.
